none: Qur'an verse text only; no commentary.

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن أبي
rows.claim: Abdullah ibn Ubay swore that he had not said, ‘If we return to Medina,’ the statement at issue in the preceding verse.
rows.anchor: حلف عبد الله بن أبي أنه ما قال لئن رجعنا إلى المدينة الآية.

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak says they swore after Hudhayfa told the Prophet that they had privately reviled him and his Companions.
rows.anchor:
وقال الضحاك:
حلفهم حين نقل حذيفة إلى الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم سبهم أصحابه

rows.speaker: قتادة وابن عباس
rows.claim: Qatada, with a report also attributed to Ibn Abbas, takes the unrealized plot as Ibn Ubay's threat that the hypocrites would expel the Prophet.
rows.anchor: قاله قتادة، وروي عن ابن عباس.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, in a report transmitted by Mujahid, identifies the plot as an attempt to kill the Prophet by a Qurayshi called al-Aswad.
rows.anchor: وقيل: بقتل الرسول، والذي هم به رجل يقال له: الأسود من قريش، رواه مجاهد عن ابن عباس.

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says fifteen men plotted at al-Aqaba to push the Prophet from his camel; Ammar led it, Hudhayfa followed, and they fled when challenged. Named plotters include Ibn Ubay, Ibn Abi Sarh, al-Jallas, and others.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: نزلت في خمسة عشر هموا بقتله وتوافقوا على أن يدفعوه عن راحلته

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another account says they planned to crown Abdullah ibn Ubay after returning from Tabuk, in rivalry with the Prophet, but failed.
rows.anchor: وقيل: همهم بما لم ينالوا، هو أن يتوجوا عبد الله بن أبي إذا رجعوا من غزوة تبوك

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that a blue-eyed man accused the Prophet and his Companions of cursing him, then fetched others who swore they had said nothing, prompting revelation.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس: كان الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم جالسا في ظل شجرة فقال: إنه سيأتيكم

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن أبي
rows.claim: One proposed ‘word of disbelief’ is Ibn Ubay's remark after a dispute between an Ansari and a Muhajir at al-Muraysiʿ, including the proverb about fattening a dog that then eats its owner.
rows.anchor: قول ابن أبي لما شاور الجهجاه الغفاري وسنان بن وبرة الجهني، وقد كسع أحدهما

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Other proposed referents for the ‘word of disbelief’ are mockery, al-Jallas's earlier remark, talk of crowning Ibn Ubay, denying that Muhammad was a prophet, or the threat about returning to Medina.
rows.anchor: أو الاستهزاء، أو قول الجلاس المتقدم، أو قولهم: نعقد التاج، أو قولهم: ليس بنبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They displayed disbelief after outwardly displaying Islam; the wording does not say ‘after their faith’ because their Islam never passed their tongues.
rows.anchor: أي أظهروا الكفر بعد إسلامهم، أي إظهار إسلامهم. ولم يأت التركيب بعد إيمانهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hamm, intending something, is weaker than firm resolve; the commentary has already noted disagreement over the intention and its object.
rows.anchor: والهم دون العزم، وتقدم الخلاف في الهام والمهموم به.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another interpretation is a plot to kill the person who carried al-Jallas's words to the Prophet; reports identify that transmitter variously as Asim ibn Adi, Hudhayfa, Umayr ibn Saʿd, or Musab.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هو هم المنافقين أو الجلاس بقتل ناقل حديث الجلاس إلى الرسول، وفي تعيين اسم الناقل خلاف

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Among the proposed identities of the transmitter al-Jallas wanted killed are Umayr ibn Saʿd, his wife's son, and, in another report, Musab.
rows.anchor: ابن امرأة الجلاس عمير بن سعد. وقيل: اسمه مصعب.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another reading is that the hypocrites plotted against the Prophet and the believers in ways they did not achieve.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هموا بالرسول والمؤمنين أشياء لم ينالوها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The complaint echoes 5:59 and 85:8: they resented the very divine favor for which they should have been grateful, turning enrichment into a pretext for hostility; poetry similarly frames benefaction as a supposed fault.
rows.anchor: هذا مثل قوله: هل تنقمون منا إلا أن آمنا وما نقموا منهم إلا أن يؤمنوا وكان حق الغني

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: The Prophet had paid Abdullah ibn Ubay a compensation that had grown due; Ikrima gives its amount as twelve thousand, while another report says it was owed to al-Jallas.
rows.anchor: وكان الرسول قد أعطى لعبد الله بن أبي دية كانت قد تغلظت له، قال عكرمة: اثنا عشر ألفا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Ansar had been poor when the Prophet came to Medina, without horses or access to war spoils; they prospered, and he told them Allah had enriched them through him.
rows.anchor: وكانت الأنصار حين قدم الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم المدينة في ضنك من العيش، لا يركبون الخيل.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question is sarcastic: their conduct makes them seem so base that they treat kindness as the only fault; cited poetry uses the same ironic complaint.
rows.anchor: وقوله: وما نقموا الجملة كلام أجري مجرى التهكم به، كما تقول: ما لي عندك ذنب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited line about the Umayyads witnesses the ironic sense of resenting people only for virtues such as forbearance and leadership.
rows.anchor: ما نقموا من بني أمية إلا ... أنهم يحلمون إن غضبوا

rows.speaker: الجلاس
rows.claim: Al-Jallas eventually admitted saying what was reported, affirmed the transmitter's truth, repented well, and is the only one of them whose accepted repentance is reported.
rows.anchor: وكان الجلاس بعد حلفه وإنكاره أن قال ما نقل عنه قد اعترف، وصدق الناقل عنه وتاب

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة والشافعي
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa and al-Shafii take the story as evidence that repentance is accepted from a zindiq who outwardly professes Islam while concealing disbelief.
rows.anchor: قيل: وفي هذا دليل على قبول توبة الزنديق المس الكفر المظهر للإيمان، وهو مذهب أبي حنيفة والشافعي.

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: Malik holds that repentance from a zindiq is not accepted once exposed, though repentance offered voluntarily before discovery is accepted without disagreement.
rows.anchor: وقال مالك: لا تقبل فإن جاء تائبا من قبل نفسه قبل أن يعثر عليه قبلت توبته بلا خلاف،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Turning away may mean abandoning repentance, faith, sincerity, or the Messenger; here it means persisting in their rejection.
rows.anchor: وإن يتولوا أي: عن التوبة، أو الإيمان، أو الإخلاص، أو الرسول. والمعنى: وإن يديموا التولي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because they openly displayed disbelief, they may be treated as belligerents, fought and killed, with their families enslaved and property taken; punishment may also begin at death or in the grave, with humiliation and fear in this life and fire in the next.
rows.anchor: إذ أظهروا الكفر، فيحل قتالهم وقتلهم، وسبي أولادهم وأزواجهم، وغنم أموالهم.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Other views locate the punishment at death before the angels of torment, in the grave, or as hardship, fear, and disgrace among believers followed by hell.
rows.anchor: وقيل: ما يصيبهم عند الموت ومعاينة ملائكة العذاب. وقيل: عذاب القبر.

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak identifies those who made the vow as Nabit ibn al-Harith, Jadd ibn Qays, Mutib ibn Qushayr, and Thalaba ibn Hatib.
rows.anchor: قال الضحاك: هم نبتل بن الحرث، وجد بن قيس، ومعتب بن قشير، وثعلبة بن حاطب

rows.speaker: الحسن ومجاهد
rows.claim: Al-Hasan and Mujahid say Mutib and Thalaba publicly made the vow together.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن ومجاهد: في معتب وثعلبة خرجا على ملأ قالا ذلك.

rows.speaker: ابن السائب
rows.claim: Ibn al-Saib says the vow came from a man of Banu Amr ibn Awf whose money in Syria was delayed; he vowed to give charity and do good if it arrived, then failed to keep the promise.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن السائب: في رجل من بني عمرو بن عوف كان له مال بالشام فأبطأ عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most commentators say the passage was revealed about Thalaba; the next segment relates the long account associated with him.
rows.anchor: والأكثر على أنها نزلت في ثعلبة،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A long account says Thalaba requested a prayer for wealth; despite advice that little he could thank God for was better, his flock multiplied, distracted him from prayer, and he called the collector's due a tax, prompting revelation.
rows.anchor: وذكروا له حديثا طويلا وقد لخصت منه: أنه سأل الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم أن يدعو الله أن يرزقه مالا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After a relative informed him of the revelation, Thalaba brought his charity, but the Prophet and then Abu Bakr, Umar, and Uthman refused it; he died during Uthman's caliphate.
rows.anchor: فأخبره قريب له بها، فجاء بصدقته إلى الرسول فلم يقبلها، فلما قبض الرسول أتى أبا بكر

rows.speaker: الأعمش
rows.claim: Al-Aamash reads both verbs with a light nūn: lanasduqanna and lanakūnanna.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الأعمش: لنصدقن ولنكونن بالنون الخفيفة فيهما،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prevalent accounts of the occasion say the vow was spoken aloud.
rows.anchor: والظاهر والمستفيض من أسباب النزول أنهم نطقوا بذلك ولفظوا به.

rows.speaker: معبد بن ثابت وفرقة
rows.claim: Maʿbad ibn Thabit and a group say the vow was only privately intended, not uttered, as the following verse about God's knowledge of secrets suggests.
rows.anchor: وقال معبد بن ثابت وفرقة: لم يتلفظوا به، وإنما هو شيء نووه في أنفسهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Among the righteous’ means financially upright through kinship, charity, Hajj, and good works; another explanation is believers seeking the afterlife.
rows.anchor: من أهل الصلاح في أموالهم بصلة الرحم والإنفاق في الخير والحج وأعمال البر.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being stingy with it means withholding its due; whenever stinginess is followed by a threat, it denotes withholding an obligatory right.
rows.anchor: بخلوا به أي: بإخراج حقه منه، وكل بخل أعقب بوعيد فهو عبارة عن منع الحق الواجب.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in ‘He caused them to inherit’ apparently refers to God, who punished their sin with a worse consequence.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن الضمير في فأعقبهم هو عائد على الله، عاقبهم على الذنب بما هو أشد منه.

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says God abandoned them when they became hypocrites, allowing hypocrisy to settle in their hearts until death because they broke their vow and lied; Abū Hayyān notes that ‘abandoned’ is Muʿtazilite wording.
rows.anchor: قال الزمخشري: خذلهم حين نافقوا، وتمكن من قلوبهم نفاقهم فلا ينفك عنها

rows.speaker: الحسن وقتادة
rows.claim: Al-Hasan and Qatada take the pronoun as referring to stinginess: stinginess left a deeply rooted hypocrisy in their hearts.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن وقتادة: الضمير في فأعقبهم للبخل، أي فأورثهم البخل نفاقا متمكنا

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Abu Muslim takes the antecedent to be their stinginess, turning away, and aversion together.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو مسلم: فأعقبهم أي البخل والتولي والإعراض.

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya offers two readings: this may be unbelieving hypocrisy, allowing Thalaba's retention to be explained by outward Islam and ambiguous evidence; or sinful hypocrisy, making his retention and the rejection of his alms a deterrent.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطية: يحتمل أن يكون نفاق كفر، ويكون تقرير ثعلبة بعد هذا النص والإبقاء عليه

rows.speaker: عمر بن عبد العزيز
rows.claim: When an official reported a man withholding zakat, Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz said to leave him and let the contempt he incurs serve as punishment.
rows.anchor: وهذا نحو ما روي أن عاملا كتب إلى عمر بن عبد العزيز أن فلانا يمنع الزكاة، فكتب إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in ‘they meet him’ apparently refers to God.
rows.anchor: والظاهر عود الضمير في: يلقونه، على الله تعالى.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternatively, they meet the recompense for their stinginess or for their deeds.
rows.anchor: وقيل: يلقون الجزاء. فقيل: جزاء بخلهم. وقيل: جزاء أفعالهم.

rows.speaker: أبو رجاء
rows.claim: Abu Raja reads yukadhdhibūn with a doubled dhāl.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو رجاء: يكذبون بالتشديد.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase does not show that they were believers before breaking the vow and only then became hypocrites: the hypocrisy is bounded as lasting until death, which does not rule out earlier hypocrisy.
rows.anchor: ولفظة: فأعقبهم نفاقا، لا تدل ولا تشعر بأنه كان مسلما، ثم لما بخل بالمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the pronoun means God, meeting Him need not imply seeing Him: scholars agree that unbelievers do not see God, and here meeting God means encountering His punishment.
rows.anchor: وإذا كان الضمير عائدا على الله فلا يكون اللقاء متضمنا رؤية الله لإجماع العلماء على أن الكفار لا يرون الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The interrogative ‘Did they not know?’ rebukes and censures them.
rows.anchor: ألم يعلموا هذا استفهام تضمن التوبيخ والتقريع.

rows.speaker: علي وأبو عبد الرحمن والحسن
rows.claim: Ali, Abu Abd al-Rahman, and al-Hasan read taʿlamu with second-person address, addressing the believers in a confirming question.
rows.anchor: وقرأ علي وأبو عبد الرحمن والحسن: تعلموا بالتاء، وهو خطاب للمؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On that reading, the verse assures believers that God exposes the hypocrites and gradually makes their concealed state known to them.
rows.anchor: وأنه تعالى فاضح المنافقين، ومعلم المؤمنين أحوالهم التي يكتمونها شيئا فشيئا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse apparently concerns all hypocrites, including those who made and broke the vow; another group restricts it to the covenant breakers.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن الآية في جميع المنافقين من عاهد وأخلف وغيرهم، وخصتها فرقة بمن عاهد

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari identifies their secret as hypocrisy and resolve to break the vow, and their private talk as religious attacks, calling charity a tax, and plotting to withhold it.
rows.anchor: فقال الزمخشري: ما أسروه من النفاق والعزم على إخلاف ما وعدوه، وما يتناجون به

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view takes their secret as concealed hypocrisy and their private talk as denigration of the Prophet and believers.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أشار بسرهم إلى ما يخفونه من النفاق، وبنجواهم إلى ما يفيضون به بينهم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A further explanation distinguishes what some say quietly to one another as their ‘secret’ from what they discuss openly together as their ‘private talk’; the interpretations are close in meaning.
rows.anchor: وقيل: سرهم ما يسار به بعضهم بعضا، ونجواهم ما تحدثوا به جهرا بينهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse concerns those who disparaged people giving charity after the Prophet urged donations.
rows.anchor: نزلت فيمن عاب المتصدقين. وكان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم حث على الصدقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abd al-Rahman gave four thousand and kept four thousand, which the Prophet blessed; Umar gave half his wealth, Asim ibn Adi one hundred wasqs, and Uthman a large donation.
rows.anchor: فتصدق عبد الرحمن بن عوف بأربعة آلاف وأمسك مثلها، فبارك له الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم فيما أمسك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Aqil gave a saʿ of dates after hired labor watering palms, keeping a saʿ for his family; another man gave a large camel with its unborn young.
rows.anchor: وأبو عقيل الأرلشي بصاع تمر، وترك لعياله صاعا، وكان آجر نفسه لسقي نخيل بهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hypocrites called the wealthy donors ostentatious and said Abu Aqil sought notice or a share of charity; some said God had no need of his small gift.
rows.anchor: فقال المنافقون: ما تصدق هؤلاء إلا رياء وسمعة، وما تصدق أبو عقيل إلا ليذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some mocked the camel donor as giving an animal better than himself; the Prophet, who noted the man's short stature and dark skin, replied three times that the man was better than them and the camel.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم: تصدق بالناقة وهي خير منه. وكان الرجل أقصر الناس قامة وأشدهم سوادا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-mutawwiʿin is the assimilated form of al-mutatawwiʿin, meaning voluntary donors such as Abd al-Rahman.
rows.anchor: وأصل المطوعين المتطوعين، فأدغمت التاء في الطاء، وهم المتبركون كعبد الرحمن وغيره.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those with only their effort are already included among the voluntary donors, but are named separately to honor their generosity despite need and toil, like Abu Aqil and Abu Khaythama.
rows.anchor: والذين لا يجدون إلا جهدهم هم مندرجون في المطوعين، ذكروا تشريفا لهم، حيث ما فاتتهم الصدقة

rows.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
rows.claim: Abu Ali al-Farisi says the second coordinated group is not included in the first, since one cannot coordinate a thing with its like; he applies this to other Qur'anic lists too.
rows.anchor: وكان أبو علي الفارسي يذهب إلى أن المعطوف في هذا وشبهه لم يندرج فيما عطف عليه قال

rows.speaker: ابن جني
rows.claim: Ibn Jinni followed his teacher Abu Ali al-Farisi, but most grammarians reject their view that the second group is excluded from the first.
rows.anchor: وإلى هذا كان يذهب تلميذه ابن جني، وأكثر الناس على خلافهما.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Some call the separate mention tajrid: the poorer donors are singled out for honor even though included in the first group.
rows.anchor: وتسمية بعضهم التجريد، جردوا بالذكر على سبيل التشريف، وقد تقدم الكلام على ذلك

rows.speaker: ابن هرمز
rows.claim: Ibn Hurmuz and a group read jahdahum with fatḥ; some say this and ḍamm are synonyms, while al-Qutabi distinguishes capacity (ḍamm) from hardship (fatḥ).
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن هرمز وجماعة: جهدهم بالفتح. فقيل: هما لغتان بمعنى واحد. وقال القتبي بالضم الطاقة

rows.speaker: الشعبي
rows.claim: Al-Shabi says ḍamm means livelihood and fatḥ means labor; another view says ḍamm denotes a small amount one can live on.
rows.anchor: وقال الشعبي: بالضم القوت، وبالفتح في العمل. وقيل: بالضم شيء قليل يعاش به.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preferred parsing makes ‘those who criticize’ the subject, attaches ‘in charity’ to ‘criticize,’ coordinates the poor donors with the voluntary donors, and coordinates ‘they mock’ with ‘they criticize’; the divine mockery and punishment form the predicate.
rows.anchor: والأحسن في الإعراب أن يكون الذين يلمزون مبتدأ، وفي الصدقات متعلق بيلمزون

rows.speaker: أبو البقاء
rows.claim: Abu al-Baqa's alternative coordination with ‘those who criticize’ would make the poor donors share the predicate and imply they too are hypocritical critics, so the author rejects it.
rows.anchor: وذكر أبو البقاء أن قوله: والذين لا يجدون، معطوف على الذين يلمزون، وهذا غير ممكن

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another suggested coordination is with ‘the believers’; the author calls that construction very remote.
rows.anchor: وقيل: والذين لا يجدون معطوف على المؤمنين، وهذا بعيد جدا.

rows.speaker: أبو البقاء
rows.claim: Abu al-Baqa offers ‘they mock’ as the predicate, with the fāʾ because the relative phrase resembles a conditional; the author objects that the predicate would merely restate the subject's meaning.
rows.anchor: قال: وخبر الأول على هذه الوجوه فيه وجهان: أحدهما فيسخرون. ودخلت الفاء لما في الذين من التشبيه بالشرط

rows.speaker: أبو البقاء
rows.claim: Abu al-Baqa's other parsing makes ‘God mocked them’ the predicate, or treats ‘those who criticize’ as the object of an omitted verb explained by ‘mocked’; an omitted predicate is also proposed.
rows.anchor: والثاني: أن الخبر سخر الله منهم، قال: وعلى هذا المعنى يجوز أن يكون الذين يلمزون

rows.speaker: أبو البقاء
rows.claim: Abu al-Baqa makes ‘among the believers’ a circumstantial phrase and attaches ‘in charity’ to ‘criticize,’ not to ‘voluntary donors,’ to avoid separating the latter from its complement.
rows.anchor: من المؤمنين حال من الضمير في المطوعين، وفي الصدقات متعلق بيلمزون، ولا يتعلق بالمطوعين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects calling the intervening circumstantial phrase foreign: a circumstantial phrase may separate a governor from its complement, as in the cited Arabic example.
rows.anchor: وليس بأجنبي لأنه حال كما قرر، وإذا كان حالا جاز الفصل بها بين العامل فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sukhriyya means mockery or ridicule.
rows.anchor: والسخرية: الاستهزاء. والظاهر أن قوله: سخر الله منهم خبر لفظا ومعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase is apparently declarative in both form and meaning, supported by the coordinated predicate that follows; another view takes its declarative form as a curse or prayer.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن قوله: سخر الله منهم خبر لفظا ومعنى، ويرجحه عطف الخبر عليه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As reciprocal mockery, God's response means He gave them respite until they thought He had neglected them; another view says He recompensed their mockery, naming the punishment by the offense, namely contempt and humiliation.
rows.anchor: ولما قال: فيسخرون منهم قال: سخر الله منهم على سبيل المقابلة، ومعناه: أمهلهم حتى ظنوا أنه أهملهم.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says this mocking occurred during the departure for the Tabuk campaign.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: وكان هذا في الخروج إلى غزوة تبوك.

rows.speaker: الأصم
rows.claim: Al-Asamm says God told the Prophet to accept their false excuses outwardly while their deeds brought their own consequences; their lasting painful punishment is in the afterlife.
rows.anchor: وقال الأصم: أمر الله نبيه صلى الله عليه وسلم أن يقبل معاذيرهم الكاذبة في الظاهر، ووبال فعلهم عليهم كما هو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning shows that slandering and mocking a believer are major sins.
rows.anchor: وفي هذه الآية دلالة على أن لمز المؤمن والسخرية منه من الكبائر، لما يعقبهما من الوعيد.

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن عبد الله بن أبي
rows.claim: When his father was ill, the righteous Abdullah ibn Abdullah ibn Ubay asked the Prophet to seek forgiveness for him; the Prophet did, and the verse followed, after which he said permission let him exceed seventy.
rows.anchor: سأل عبد الله بن عبد الله بن أبي رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وكان رجلا صالحا أن يستغفر لأبيه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another occasion says the hypocrites requested prayer for forgiveness after the verse threatened them with divine mockery and painful punishment.
rows.anchor: وقيل: لما نزل سخر الله منهم ولهم عذاب أليم، سألوا الرسول أن يستغفر لهم فنزلت.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the second occasion account, the pronouns refer either to the people just mentioned or to all hypocrites.
rows.anchor: وعلى هذا فالضمائر عائدة على الذين سبق ذكرهم، أو على جميع المنافقين قولان.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The imperative addressed to the Prophet apparently gives him a choice: seek forgiveness or refrain, although God then says even seventy prayers will not bring forgiveness.
rows.anchor: والخطاب بالأمر للرسول، والظاهر أن المراد بهذا الكلام التخيير

rows.speaker: عمر
rows.claim: When Umar objected that God had forbidden praying for an enemy, the Prophet answered that He had not forbidden it but had given him a choice.
rows.anchor: وقد قال له عمر: كيف تستغفروا لعدو الله وقد نهاك الله عن الاستغفار لهم؟

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view takes the imperative as a conditional statement: whether the Prophet seeks forgiveness or not, God will not forgive them, like the command to spend willingly or reluctantly in 9:53; al-Tabari and al-Zamakhshari prefer this reading.
rows.anchor: وقيل: لفظه أمر ومعناه الشرط، بمعنى إن استغفرت أو لم تستغفر لن يغفر الله

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari explains the imperative as a report with conditional force, parallel to ‘spend willingly or reluctantly’ in 9:53, and points to the rhetorical point of using a command form.
rows.anchor: وقد ذكرنا أن هذا الأمر في معنى الخبر كأنه قيل: لن يغفر الله لهم استغفرت أم لم تستغفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command-form-as-report reading is likened to ‘whoever is in error, let the Most Merciful extend him,’ whose sense is an assertion about what will happen.
rows.anchor: كقوله: قل من كان في الضلالة فليمدد له الرحمن مدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited poetic command ‘harm us or treat us kindly’ means that the beloved's response will not change the speaker's standing, paralleling forgiveness whether the Prophet intercedes or not.
rows.anchor: أسيئي بنا أو أحسبني لا ملومة أي: لن يغفر الله لهم استغفرت لهم أو لا تستغفر

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says the imperative lets a lover test whether kindness and cruelty alter the beloved's state; similarly, ask forgiveness or refrain and see whether the result changes.
rows.anchor: امتحني لطف محلك عندي، وقوة محبتي لك، وعامليني بالإساءة والإحسان، وانظري هل تتفاوت حالي

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Zamakhshari's analogy continues: spend and see whether it is accepted, or ask forgiveness and see whether the outcome differs; the command has the force of a test.
rows.anchor: وكذلك المعنى أنفقوا وانظروا هل يتقبل منكم، واستغفر لهم أو لا تستغفر لهم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Other explanations say the command intensifies despair, as though seeking were required or abstaining forbidden, or simply means that seeking forgiveness and refraining are equivalent.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هو أمر مبالغة في الإياس ومعناه: أنك لو طلبت الاستغفار لهم طلب المأمور

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: To explain how the Prophet could pray for unbelievers, one view says he did so to win many hypocrites to sincere faith.
rows.anchor: أحدها: أن ذلك كان على سبيل التأليف ليخلص إيمان كثير منهم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is reported that after the Prophet prayed for Ibn Salul, lent him his garment, and attended his funeral, a thousand Khazraj converted after seeing him seek blessing through the garment.
rows.anchor: وقد روي أنه لما استغفر لابن سلول وكساه ثوبه، وصلى عليه، أسلم ألف من الخزرج

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation is that the Prophet acted to comfort Ibn Salul's son and the believers among the hypocrites; this resembles the effort to win them over.
rows.anchor: وقيل: فعل ذلك تطييبا لقلب ولده ومن أسلم منهم، وهذا قريب مما قبله.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Believers asked him to pray for hypocrite relatives while alive, hoping they would become sincere, and after death hoping for pardon; God then forbade it and ended their hope.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إنما استغفر لقوم منهم على ظاهر إسلامهم من غير أن يحقق خروجهم عن الإسلام

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A view says the Prophet prayed for some because their outward Islam was known but their apostasy was not; it is rejected because God had declared their disbelief.
rows.anchor: ورد هذا القول بأنه تعالى أخبر بأنهم كفروا فلا يصح أن يقال إنه غير عالم بكفرهم.

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Razi says the closest connection is Ibn Abbas's view that the people who mocked the donors were the same ones who asked the Prophet to pray for them.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو عبد الله الرازي: الأقرب في تعلق هذه الآية بما قبلها ما ذكره ابن عباس

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Razi argues the Prophet would not begin praying for hypocrites and then be stopped: Islamic law already prohibited praying for unbelievers, as in the exception to Abraham's promise to seek forgiveness for his father.
rows.anchor: الأول: أن المنافق كافر، وقد ظهر في شرعه عليه السلام أن الاستغفار للكافر لا يجوز

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Razi's second argument is that another person's prayer cannot benefit someone persisting in sin and wrongdoing.
rows.anchor: الثاني: أن استغفار الغير للغير لا ينفعه إذا كان ذلك الغير مصرا على القبيح والمعصية.

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله الرازي
rows.claim: His third argument is that interceding for hypocrites would encourage them to persist in sin.
rows.anchor: الثالث: أن إقدامه على الاستغفار للمنافقين يجري مجرى إغرائهم بالإقدام على الذنب.

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله الرازي
rows.claim: His fourth argument is that an unanswered prophetic prayer would appear rejected by God and diminish the Prophet's standing.
rows.anchor: الرابع: أنه إذا كان لا يجيبه بقي دعاء الرسول مردودا عند الله، وذلك يوجب نقصان منصبه

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله الرازي
rows.claim: His fifth argument is that if the Prophet's prayer were accepted, one request would suffice as much as many; seventy is not a threshold after which forgiveness becomes possible.
rows.anchor: الخامس: أن هذا الدعاء لو كان مقبولا من الرسول لكان قليله مثل كثيره في حصول الإجابة

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Razi says the stated cause, their disbelief and wickedness, proves the point: no number of prayers benefits them while they persist in disbelief, so the number removes hope rather than setting a limit.
rows.anchor: والذي يؤكد ذلك قوله تعالى في الآية: ذلك بأنهم كفروا. فبين أن العلة التي لأجلها لا ينفعهم

rows.speaker: الأزهري
rows.claim: Al-Azhari and other linguists say seventy is the pluralized seven used for abundance, not an exact count; Arabs amplify with seven, seventy, and seven hundred in units, tens, and hundreds.
rows.anchor: وقال الأزهري في جماعة من أهل اللغة: السبعون هنا جمع السبعة المستعملة للكثرة

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says seventy functions like a proverbial expression for a very large number; Ali's verse uses seventy thousand to describe the army he will summon.
rows.anchor: قال الزمخشري: والسبعون جار مجرى المثل في كلامهم للتكثير. قال علي رضي الله تعالى عنه

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya says seventy often marks an endpoint or satisfactory limit for a large number, as with Moses' chosen men and the people at al-Aqaba.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطية: وأما تمثيله بالسبعين دون غيرها من الأعداد فلأنه عدد كثيرا ما يجيء غاية
